---
title: "AlphaGenome Real-versus-Synthetic Background Comparison"
subtitle: "`r params$analysis_name` | GRCh38 chromosome learning curves"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    number_sections: true
    theme: cosmo
params:
  real_metrics_path: null
  synthetic_metrics_path: null
  analysis_name: null
  positive_class: null
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE,
                      fig.width=9, fig.height=7, dpi=120)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(gt); library(scales)})
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size=12) +
          theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank(), legend.position="bottom"))
background_colors <- c(Real="#0072B2", Synthetic="#D55E00")
background_shapes <- c(Real=16, Synthetic=17)
```

```{r inputs, include=FALSE}
required_params <- c("real_metrics_path", "synthetic_metrics_path",
                     "analysis_name", "positive_class")
for (name in required_params)
  if (is.null(params[[name]]) || !nzchar(params[[name]]))
    stop("Missing parameter: ", name)

read_metrics <- function(path, expected_kind) {
  path <- normalizePath(path, mustWork=TRUE)
  x <- read.delim(path, sep="\t", stringsAsFactors=FALSE, check.names=FALSE)
  required <- c("model", "dataset", "negative_kind", "checkpoint_index",
                "n_training_total", "split", "n_evaluation_positive",
                "n_evaluation_negative", "n_evaluation_total", "auroc", "auprc")
  missing <- setdiff(required, names(x))
  if (length(missing)) stop("Missing columns in ", path, ": ", paste(missing, collapse=", "))
  if (nrow(x) != 63) stop("Expected 63 rows in ", path, "; found ", nrow(x))
  if (!all(x$model == "alphagenome")) stop("Non-AlphaGenome rows in ", path)
  if (!all(x$negative_kind == expected_kind)) stop("Background-type mismatch in ", path)
  x
}

real <- read_metrics(params$real_metrics_path, "real")
synthetic <- read_metrics(params$synthetic_metrics_path, "synthetic")
if (!identical(unique(real$dataset), unique(synthetic$dataset)))
  stop("Dataset mismatch between real and synthetic inputs")

metrics <- bind_rows(real, synthetic) |>
  mutate(
    Background=factor(recode(negative_kind, real="Real", synthetic="Synthetic"),
                      levels=c("Real", "Synthetic")),
    Split=factor(recode(split, train_100="Full training pool",
                        validation="Validation", test="Test"),
                 levels=c("Full training pool", "Validation", "Test")),
    ranking_error=1-auroc
  ) |>
  arrange(Background, Split, checkpoint_index)

metric_limits <- function(v) {
  span <- diff(range(v, na.rm=TRUE)); pad <- max(span*.08, .002)
  range(v, na.rm=TRUE) + c(-pad, pad)
}

curve_plot <- function(metric, title, label) {
  ggplot(metrics, aes(n_training_total, .data[[metric]], color=Background,
                      shape=Background, group=Background)) +
    geom_line(linewidth=.9) + geom_point(size=2.1) +
    facet_grid(Split ~ ., scales="free_x") +
    scale_color_manual(values=background_colors) +
    scale_shape_manual(values=background_shapes) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels=comma, expand=expansion(mult=c(.02,.03))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim=metric_limits(metrics[[metric]])) +
    labs(title=title, x="Cumulative training observations", y=label,
         color="Negative background", shape="Negative background")
}
```

# Scope and interpretation

This report compares AlphaGenome performance for the GRCh38
`r params$analysis_name` task when trained and evaluated with real genomic versus
synthetic shuffled negative backgrounds. `r params$positive_class` sequences are
label 1 and the corresponding background sequences are label 0.

Both datasets are internally class-balanced. The real and synthetic benchmarks
are not perfectly locus-matched because a foreground was retained only when the
corresponding background generator produced an acceptable negative. Consequently,
the curves compare two closely related balanced benchmarks rather than a strictly
paired estimate of the background-generation effect.

Chr1 is validation, chr2 is held-out test, and independent learning-curve models
cumulatively add chr3 through chrX.

```{r dataset-summary}
metrics |>
  distinct(Background, Split, n_evaluation_positive,
           n_evaluation_negative, n_evaluation_total) |>
  rename(Positives=n_evaluation_positive, Negatives=n_evaluation_negative,
         `Total observations`=n_evaluation_total) |>
  arrange(Background, Split) |>
  gt(groupname_col="Background") |>
  tab_header(title="Evaluation datasets") |>
  fmt_integer(columns=c(Positives, Negatives, `Total observations`))
```

# AUROC learning curves

```{r auroc}
curve_plot("auroc", "AlphaGenome AUROC by negative-background type", "AUROC")
```

# Average-precision learning curves

```{r auprc}
curve_plot("auprc", "AlphaGenome average precision by negative-background type",
           "Average Precision")
```

# AUROC ranking-error curves

```{r ranking}
curve_plot("ranking_error", "AlphaGenome AUROC ranking error by negative-background type",
           "1 - AUROC")
```

# Final-model comparison

```{r final-model}
metrics |>
  filter(checkpoint_index == max(checkpoint_index)) |>
  select(Background, Split, n_training_total, n_evaluation_total, auroc, auprc) |>
  rename(`Training observations`=n_training_total,
         `Evaluation observations`=n_evaluation_total,
         AUROC=auroc, `Average Precision`=auprc) |>
  arrange(Background, Split) |>
  gt(groupname_col="Background") |>
  tab_header(title="Final chr3-through-chrX AlphaGenome models") |>
  fmt_integer(columns=c(`Training observations`, `Evaluation observations`)) |>
  fmt_number(columns=c(AUROC, `Average Precision`), decimals=3)
```

# Reproducibility notes

- Every learning-curve checkpoint was trained independently.
- Real and synthetic runs used the same AlphaGenome architecture and fixed training hyperparameters.
- Metric axes are shared across background types within each figure.
- Test data were used only for final evaluation.
- Differences cannot be attributed solely to the background generator because retained foreground loci are not perfectly paired.
